s: Bhava Viveka served as Acharya in which of the following Buddhist Viharas?
x:
Bhavaviveka (Bhavya) was one of the greatest philosophers of the Mahayana Madhyamaka School of Buddhism. He served as an Acharya at Sriparvatam, an important Buddhist centre located in the Nagarjunakonda region. Sriparvatam was an internationally renowned centre of Buddhist education where monks and scholars from India and abroad pursued higher learning. Bhavaviveka composed several philosophical works explaining and defending the Madhyamaka doctrine through logical reasoning. His writings greatly influenced later Buddhist philosophy in India, Tibet and East Asia.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).

s: Who described Sri Parvataswamy as Buddha?
x:
The German epigraphist F. Kielhorn expressed the view that Sri Parvataswamy referred to Lord Buddha. This interpretation was based on inscriptions and historical evidence relating to Sri Parvata (Nagarjunakonda region), which was one of the greatest centres of Mahayana Buddhism in ancient India. Since the region was closely associated with Buddhist monasteries and scholars such as Acharya Nagarjuna, Kielhorn identified Sri Parvataswamy with Buddha. Although later historians have offered different interpretations, APPSC recognizes Kielhorn as the scholar associated with this view.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).

s: Which Chinese traveler wrote that he saw students memorizing "Suhrlekha" in India?
x:
The Chinese Buddhist pilgrim Itsing (Yijing) recorded that Buddhist students in India memorized "Suhrlekha", a famous work attributed to Acharya Nagarjuna. Suhrlekha (Letter to a Friend) is a moral and philosophical text advising righteous conduct, ethical living and Buddhist principles. Itsing's account highlights the popularity of Nagarjuna's writings in Buddhist education.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).

s: "Hariti" was the tutelary deity of whom?
x:
Hariti, originally regarded as a protector of children in Buddhist tradition, became an important tutelary deity of the Ikshvakus. Numerous sculptures and inscriptions from Nagarjunakonda indicate the popularity of Hariti worship during the Ikshvaku period. She was revered as the guardian deity associated with prosperity, fertility and child protection.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).

s: Which Ikshvaku king tried to make the intelligentsia partners in agricultural development?
x:
Sri Chantamula I, the founder of the Ikshvaku dynasty, encouraged Brahmins and learned scholars to participate in agricultural development by granting them land (Brahmadeya grants). These grants promoted the cultivation of new lands, improved agricultural productivity and contributed to the spread of Vedic culture in the Krishna valley.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).
n: Policy – Land grants to scholars for agricultural development

s: During whose reign did Buddhism receive the greatest patronage in the Ikshvaku Kingdom?
x:
The reign of Veerapurushadatta is regarded as the golden age of Buddhism in the Ikshvaku Kingdom. His queens and royal women generously patronized Buddhist monasteries, stupas and viharas at Nagarjunakonda (Vijayapuri). Numerous inscriptions record donations made during his reign.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).
n: Golden Age of Buddhism under Ikshvakus
